pr_title: changefeedccl: signal changeAggregator shutdown from the kvfeed
pr_body:
During acceptance testing, we observed that changefeeds did not
correctly restart on primary key changes and did not correctly stop
when schema_change_policy was set to 'stop' when the changeFrontier
and changeAggregator were running on different nodes (most production
changefeeds).

The root cause of this was a bad assumption in the changeAggregator
shutdown logic. Namely, we assumed that the changeAggregator (and kv
feed) would see context cancellations as a result of the
changeFrontier moving to draining. However, this is not guaranteed.

When the changeFrontier moves to draining, all of its inputs will be
drained. But, a DrainRequest message is only sent to the input lazily
when the next message is received from that input.

In this case of a schema change, the kv feed would stop sending
messages to the changeAggregator and thus no further messages will be
sent to the changeFrontier and the drain request is not triggered.

With this change, we now shut down the changeAggregator when the
kvfeed indicates that no more messages will be returned.

Fixes #68791

Release note (enterprise change): Fixed a bug where CHANGEFEEDs would
fail to correctly handle a primary key change.

issue_context.title: changefeeds fail to restart/exit when encountering some schema changes
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Certain schema changes should result in a changefeed restart:

- `ALTER TABLE .. SET LOCALITY REGIONAL BY ROW`
- `ALTER TABLE .. ALTER PRIMARY KEY ...`

The restart is required to ensure that we start new rangefeeds on the new index that that these schema changes create.

Further when the user specifies `schema_change_policy=stop` schema changes such as `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN .. DEFUALT ..` should result in the changefeed permanently exiting.

However, we've observed some cases where the changefeed fails to exit or restart correctly.  In these cases, the changefeed appears to still be running, but no newly inserted rows or resolved timestamps will be sent to the sink.

Internally in such cases, what we've found so far is that the `kvFeed` encounters the schema change, forwards Resolved spans with the appropriate schema change boundary type set to the `changeAggregator` and attempts to exit. Further the `changeAggregator` correctly forwards the schema change boundary to the `changeFrontier`. The changeFrontier advances to the boundary and attempts to exit.  However, it appears that at this point we can become deadlocked (the exact cause of the deadlock is not known).

It appears to me that:

- the `changeFrontier` has entered a draining state and is waiting for its inputs (`changeAggregator`) to drain:

```
goroutine 17682 [chan receive, 6 minutes]:
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfra.(*RowChannel).Next(0xc003ed01e0, 0xc003747490, 0x1, 0x1, 0x4e1a45)
        /go/src/github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfra/base.go:508 +0x4a
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfra.(*ProcessorBaseNoHelper).DrainHelper(0xc0033aea80, 0xc002c2a5d8)
        /go/src/github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/sql/execinfra/processorsbase.go:571 +0xac
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl.(*changeFrontier).Next(0xc0033aea80, 0x34d10769, 0xc000bd0000, 0xc0044c23c0, 0xc000ba9380)
```

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/4c4135e7f4edc7142051ada818aeaad0e2bed710/pkg/sql/execinfra/processorsbase.go#L567-L571

- The `changeAggregator` is waiting for an event from its channel buffer (which the kvFeed is the writer for):

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/4c4135e7f4edc7142051ada818aeaad0e2bed710/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/changefeed_processors.go#L466-L469

- The `kvFeed`, however, is attempting to shut down after encountering the schemachange. It is not going to be writing to the channel that `changeAggregator` is waiting on:

```
goroutine 17061 [chan receive, 6 minutes]:
github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/kvfeed.Run(0x66a3068, 0xc0036b92c0, 0xc000872000, 0xc00176f380, 0xc00174a348, 0xc00174a348, 0x0, 0xc000c68d70, 0x4fff280, 0xc000ac4000, ...)
        /go/src/github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/kvfeed/kv_feed.go:112 +0x7b6
```

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/e723a85739a2e1b514f5de3221a2177a3a37d0e6/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/kvfeed/kv_feed.go#L106-L115

So, we'll sit in this state until ca.Ctx is cancelled, which doesn't happen.

**To Reproduce**

What did you do? Describe in your own words.

If possible, provide steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Set up CockroachDB cluster with non-trivial latency between the nodes. For example, a node in us-east1, us-west1, and europe-west2.  In the following, all commands are run from the us-east1 node.

2. Setup a kafka sink (or any other sink where you can easily observe the changefeed output).

3. Setup table and changefeed

```sql
CREATE DATABASE test;
\c test
ALTER DATABASE test PRIMARY REGION "us-west1";
ALTER DATABASE test ADD region "us-east1";
ALTER DATABASE test ADD region "europe-west2";

CREATE TABLE tab1 (pk INT PRIMARY KEY, a INT UNIQUE NOT NULL, b INT);
INSERT INTO tab1 VALUES(1, 11, 3);
INSERT INTO tab1 VALUES(2, 22, 3);
INSERT INTO tab1 VALUES(3, 33, 4);
CREATE CHANGEFEED FOR TABLE tab1 INTO 'kafka://10.142.15.195:9092' WITH updated, resolved, confluent_schema_registry = 'http://10.142.15.195:8081', format = 'experimental_avro';
```

4. You should observe the 3 rows being send to the sink followed by resolved timestamps.
5. Do the schema change:

```
ALTER TABLE tab1 ALTER PRIMARY KEY USING COLUMNS(a);
```

6. If you trigger the issue, you will observe resolved timestamps right up to the timestamp of the schema change.  The changefeed job will still show as "running" in the jobs table.  But further writes will not be sent to the sink.

**Expected behavior**

The changefeedFrontier, changefeedAggregator, and kvFeed should completely exit and either restart or report as a failed job depending on the situation.

Follow up:

This only seem to reproduce for me when the the `changeAggregator` and `changeFrontier` live on different nodes.  To help ensure this, I make sure that the leaseholder for the range for the table is on node 2, and then I start the changefeed from node 1.

review_comments: do you know why we're just not returning an error here?

I do not.  I've read through the code and I believe that it would _currently_ be OK to return early from here because the unbuffered channel we use is already acting as a synchronisation point. I've removed the <-ctx.Done() and didn't see any test failures, but I want to run that under stress a bit more just in case I missed something in my read through.
I've updated the comment here to explain why we aren't currently just returning.
would it be better to query jobs table to see if the job exited w/ this error?
This is how we wait for schema change errors in a few other tests that have been rather reliable.
I've opted to return the error directly instead since closing the sink is required for correct execution.
